cases.setup_script:
set -e
export TZ=UTC0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Fixture GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=fixture@example.test GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Fixture GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=fixture@example.test
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2020-03-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2020-03-01T00:00:00Z'
/usr/bin/ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C fixture -f "$HOME/key"
/usr/bin/git init -q -b main signed
/usr/bin/git -C signed config gc.auto 0
/usr/bin/git -C signed config maintenance.auto false
printf 'signed\n' >signed/file
/usr/bin/git -C signed add file
/usr/bin/git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingKey="$HOME/key" commit -q -S -m signed
/usr/bin/git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingKey="$HOME/key" tag -s -m signed signed-tag
cases.oracle: Pinned Debian Git 2.47.3 and OpenSSH 10.0: a missing configured revocation file emits a warning and verifies a valid allowed signer; observed again by the reference side of every run. The candidate side is held to the documented fail-closed contract of this build.
cases.comparison: Missing revocation path only. Both sides first verify the same signed commit without a revocation file and must report a good signature for the allowed signer. With gpg.ssh.revocationFile naming a missing file, the reference side must show Debian Git warning ('ssh signing revocation file configured but not found:') and still verifying (status 0, good signature); the candidate side must show this build stopping fail-closed: nonzero status, the line 'Cannot verify SSH signature with a configured revocation file.', and no good-signature line. Each side prints missing-revocation-file=recorded-behavior only when its own recorded behavior is observed, and its raw observations otherwise. That difference is deliberate and recorded, so it is asserted on each side rather than compared between them. The r3 case that expected system Git to reject a missing file is retired.
cases.reference_script:
export TZ=UTC0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
read -r kt kk comment < "$HOME/key.pub"
printf 'fixture@example.test %s %s\n' "$kt" "$kk" > "$HOME/allowed"
/usr/bin/rm -f "$HOME/revoked"
# Control: without a revocation file configured the signed commit verifies for the allowed signer.
git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile="$HOME/allowed" verify-commit HEAD >"$HOME/control.out" 2>"$HOME/control.err"; control=$?
if [[ $control == 0 ]] && /usr/bin/grep -F 'Good "git" signature for fixture@example.test' "$HOME/control.out" "$HOME/control.err" >/dev/null; then echo 'control=accepted'; else echo "control=rejected($control)"; fi
git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile="$HOME/allowed" -c gpg.ssh.revocationFile="$HOME/revoked" verify-commit HEAD >"$HOME/revoked.out" 2>"$HOME/revoked.err"; rc=$?
if /usr/bin/grep -F 'Good "git" signature' "$HOME/revoked.out" "$HOME/revoked.err" >/dev/null; then good=yes; else good=no; fi
# Debian Git: a configured revocation file that does not exist is warned about and verification proceeds.
if /usr/bin/grep -F 'ssh signing revocation file configured but not found:' "$HOME/revoked.err" >/dev/null; then warning=yes; else warning=no; fi
if [[ $rc == 0 && $warning == yes && $good == yes ]]; then echo 'missing-revocation-file=recorded-behavior'; else echo "missing-revocation-file=unexpected reference rc=$rc warning=$warning good=$good"; fi
/usr/bin/rm -rf signed
cases.candidate_script:
export TZ=UTC0 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
read -r kt kk comment < "$HOME/key.pub"
printf 'fixture@example.test %s %s\n' "$kt" "$kk" > "$HOME/allowed"
/usr/bin/rm -f "$HOME/revoked"
# Control: without a revocation file configured the signed commit verifies for the allowed signer.
git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile="$HOME/allowed" verify-commit HEAD >"$HOME/control.out" 2>"$HOME/control.err"; control=$?
if [[ $control == 0 ]] && /usr/bin/grep -F 'Good "git" signature for fixture@example.test' "$HOME/control.out" "$HOME/control.err" >/dev/null; then echo 'control=accepted'; else echo "control=rejected($control)"; fi
git -C signed -c gpg.format=ssh -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile="$HOME/allowed" -c gpg.ssh.revocationFile="$HOME/revoked" verify-commit HEAD >"$HOME/revoked.out" 2>"$HOME/revoked.err"; rc=$?
if /usr/bin/grep -F 'Good "git" signature' "$HOME/revoked.out" "$HOME/revoked.err" >/dev/null; then good=yes; else good=no; fi
# This build: a configured revocation file that cannot be read stops verification (fail-closed).
if /usr/bin/grep -Fx 'Cannot verify SSH signature with a configured revocation file.' "$HOME/revoked.out" "$HOME/revoked.err" >/dev/null; then refusal=yes; else refusal=no; fi
if [[ $rc != 0 && $refusal == yes && $good == no ]]; then echo 'missing-revocation-file=recorded-behavior'; else echo "missing-revocation-file=unexpected candidate rc=$rc refusal=$refusal good=$good"; fi
/usr/bin/rm -rf signed
